paper.title: Towards Domain Adaptive Neural Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Cross-domain contextual bandit setting (zero-shot target regret)
unmapped: Two domains (source and target) with distribution shift; feedback is only collected in the source domain, target-domain contexts are observed without rewards
Regret measured in the target domain with a fixed policy learned from the source domain (zero-shot regret over N hypothetical rounds)
Reward = <theta*, phi*(x)> with unknown ground-truth neural encoder phi* (domain-specific)
settings.definition_quote: one can only collect feedback (reward) from the source domain, but not from the target domain... The goal in our cross-domain contextual bandits is to learn a policy of choosing actions $\hat{a}_{i}$ in the target domain to minimize the target-domain \textbf{zero-shot regret} for $N$ (hypothetical) future rounds

bound.expression_latex: R_S + 2\epsilon_S(h) + N \hat{d}_{H\Delta H}(S,T) + \psi + C + \sum_i |\langle\hat\theta,\hat\phi(x^T_{i,\hat a_i})\rangle| + \sum_i 1[a_i^*\neq\hat a_i]|\langle\hat\theta,\hat\phi(x^S_{i,\hat a_i})\rangle|

symbols.eps_S: source-domain regression error epsilon_S(h) (sum of absolute reward prediction errors on chosen actions)
symbols.d_HdH: empirical H-Delta-H divergence for regression between source and target
symbols.psi: combined source+target error of the optimal joint hypothesis h*
symbols.C_const: sum_i alpha*kappa_i^T + 1[a_i* != a_hat_i] sum_i alpha*kappa_i^S (exploration-bonus terms claimed negligible)
symbols.P_pred: predicted-reward term: sum_i |<theta_hat, phi_hat(x^T_{i,a_hat_i})>| + sum_i 1[a_i* != a_hat_i] |<theta_hat, phi_hat(x^S_{i,a_hat_i})>|

conditions: target actions chosen by the UCB rule using the source-trained model

source.label: thm:target_regret_bound

results.notes: Data-dependent decomposition bound, not an explicit rate; N is the horizon (mapped to T). Restated as Theorem 2 in appendix. Paper informally argues C vanishes and the bound is sublinear (via Neural-LinUCB O(sqrt N) source regret and Adam), but no explicit rate is proved. Regret defined with absolute values on noiseless means; recorded as pathwise realized regret.
